text:
ajay: heads up — cost jumped ~28% last week from sustained interactive usage on spot GPUs. thinking we need a multi-tenant fair-spill plan to protect low-latency endpoints while still getting spot savings for batch.
maria: +1. can we separate via queue affinity? interactive -> reserved or guaranteed slices, batch -> spot pools with prefilling overnight. also consider graceful drain window for spots.
sophie: curious on SLA impacts. how long are we willing to tail latency for interactive when we fall back? 200ms SLO today.
charlie: proposed quick sketch:
- interactive queue: reserved-min 30% of capacity in peak hours, burst to spot only if latency < SLO for 10m
- batch queue: preemptible-first, run checkpoints every 15m, auto-retry with exponential backoff on preemption
charlie: config snippet (rough):
```yaml
queues:
  interactive:
    min_reserved: 0.3
    max_burst_spot: 0.5
    latency_slo_ms: 200
  batch:
    priority: low
    spot_only: true
    checkpoint_interval: 900
``` 
maria: love the YAML. also add per-tenant weights so one team doesn't hog reserved share.
ajay: region note — us-west1 has 80% of our V100/4090 avail this week, but preempt churn spiked in europe-west1. suggest cross-region fallback policy with cost floor.
sophie: can we set a cost guardrail? e.g., if on-demand spend > X% projected, throttle noncritical training and shift to off-peak windows.
charlie: yep — implement a daily off-peak shift window (00:00–06:00 local) for heavy batch jobs. jobs can opt-in via `--time-window offpeak`.
infra-bot: [metric] spot_churn_rate increased from 3.4% -> 9.1% last 72h in europe-west1 :warning:
oncall-bot: reminder: runbook for mass preemptions -> /runbooks/spot-drain; notify #incidents if > 20% disruption.
maria: interruption handling: prefer small MSS-style checkpoints over single huge checkpoints; incremental upload to s3 works best.
ajay: tradeoffs: smaller checkpoints mean longer wall-clock but faster restart. good for long training; for interactive ephemeral state we need KV-cache persistence strategy.
charlie: technical approach for interactive fallback:
1) probe latency on reserved slice every 30s
2) if probe fails or latency > SLO, mark route -> fallback model variant (quantized) in same region
3) only spill to remote region as last resort (route costs accounting)
sophie: how do we account for cross-region egress in billing? need to tag and surface in console per-route cost.
maria: ops: add fairshare token bucket per-team, refill based on weekly quota. teams can trade tokens for burst minutes during sprint demos :moneybag:.
ajay: can infra team draft a rollout plan? i'd like a gradual rollout: week 1 dry-run (metrics only), week 2 canary on 10% of traffic, week 3 full enable for non-critical namespaces.
charlie: I'll put up a PR with autoscaler changes + drain handler and the queue config. ETA EOD tomorrow.
maria: ops will prepare token-bucket limits and off-peak schedule.
sophie: i'll update SLO docs and add cost alerts to the console dashboard.
ajay: action items: charlie PR, maria token quotas, sophie SLO+alerts. ping @oncall-bot if we see >5% preempt rate during rollout. thanks all :thumbsup:
